newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes release of Nigeria activists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes release of Nigeria activists.

text.p: The United States said Friday it welcomed the release of three Nigerian human rights activists and hoped all other political prisoners would be freed promptly.
Gani Fawehinmi, Femi Falana and Femi Aborishade were freed Wednesday during a visit of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group.
Nigeria was suspended in November 1996 from the 53-member Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies after the military government hanged nine minority rights activists.

"We hope it (the release of the three activists) leads to the prompt release of all other individuals held without charge or for essentially political purposes," State Department spokesman Glen Davies said in a statement.

"We thrust that Mr. Fawehinmi, Mr. Falana and Mr. Aborishade will be permitted to return to their families and their work, including political and human rights activities, without harassment or rearrest," Davies said.
